lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: You'll be the new tenant, then. Bait shop's yours till somebody says otherwise.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Rod's on the hook by the door. Your aunt's, it was. Go on, end of the dock.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Hold to cast, let go in the bright bit. Bring me three fish and I'll show you how we do things.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Three fish, love. End of the dock. I'll be right here, pretending not to watch.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Three! And none of them looking at you funny. Good start.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: I'll buy what you catch, right here at the stall. Fair prices. Mostly fair.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Half the village eats what comes off this dock. Lately it's been… thin.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Sell me eight fish. The bigger the better. The odder the better, honestly.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Eight fish for the stall. Bring them here and I'll do the sums.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: That'll feed the Pollards and then some. Here, you've earned a look at the good shelf.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: And the notice board by the stall's got odd jobs, if you want more coin. Folk pay well for strange requests.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: That driftwood stick will snap the first time something with opinions bites.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Harbour Rod. Four hundred and fifty. I'll even throw in some worms.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Harbour Rod's on the good shelf. Four-fifty. I don't haggle. Much.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Now you look like you mean it. Worms are in the tin. Don't open it indoors.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: Look! I drew it before I saw it. That means it's real. That's how it works.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: It's pink and it bites sunsets. It lives near the cove or the Teeth. Catch it? Please?

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: The pink one! Near the cove or the Teeth. It likes sunsets best.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: It looks EXACTLY like my drawing! Except it has fewer legs. I'll fix that.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: The light on Gull Point's been dark since the keeper went down. Down, I said. Not away.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: A lamp like that won't take ordinary oil. It wants a light the sea made.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Lampjaw. After the sun's gone. Bring me one.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Lampjaw only shows once the sun's gone. Be patient. The sea is.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: There. Still warm. Hold onto it, it'll want to go home.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Up the stairs, all the way. Put the light where the light goes.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: And when it catches, don't look at the water. Not straight away.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: I'll row you out to Gull Point when you're ready. Just say.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: There she is. Hearthbay's been holding its breath a long while.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: You saw it, didn't you. In the water. Two of them.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Good. Then you're the keeper now. Nobody chooses it. Take the skiff, it was hers.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: She's light on the helm. Push her on and she goes, let her be and she glides. Never cast till she's settled.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: South-west of here there's an isle with a kettle on it. The keeper took her tea there, tides she wanted quiet.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Go and see if it's still warm. It will be. That's the part I don't care for.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Kettle Isle. West of the cove, out past its mouth. You'll know the beach.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Warm, was it. Twelve winters on a bare rock, and warm.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Keep it. Her things go to whoever keeps the light.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: So he's given you the skiff. Good. It's sat at that dock like a held breath.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: South-west there's three black rocks, the Teeth. Deep water. Nothing off them has reached my stall in a long while.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Bring me a Twofold Flounder. And don't let it look at you with both faces at once.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: The Teeth, south-west past the sandbar. Flounder sit deep, so give it line.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Oh, that's the one. Look at it. Looking at us.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: My sister brought these in by the basket. I don't know why I said that. I haven't got a sister.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Word's got round that there's fish on my stall again. Proper fish, deep-water fish. I've had people at the door before light.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Keep it full for me. Six thousand coins' worth across this counter, and the village eats well till the cold.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: There's a hat in the back that's been waiting for somebody. I'd say whose, if I could think.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Keep the stall full. Deep water pays best, so mind the Teeth.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Six thousand. I've not written a number like that in this book since... well. There's no since. It's a new book.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Here. It fits you. I knew it would, and I can't think how I knew.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Your aunt kept lantern pots off this dock. A light in a basket. Fish swim in to look, and can't think how to leave.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: There's one left in the shed. Set it in the water and it fishes while you do. Only fish it's seen you catch, mind. It learns from you.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: And it only works while you're about. Leave it a night and you'll find it just as you left it. Don't ask me why.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Set the pot in the water, give it a while, then go and haul it up. It won't come to you.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: There. Small fish, pot fish. But they sell, and you never lifted a rod.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: I've more pots if you want them, and brighter wicks. I'll put them out on the stall.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: Biscuit isn't anybody's. I asked. She said she'd think about it if there was fish.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: She wants one of each. A butterperch, a pebble goby and a coral snapper. The ones off her own dock. I drew them so you'd know. She sat on the drawing.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: She keeps looking at your boat. She's never been on a boat. I think she's been on yours, though. Before.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: One of each! Butterperch, pebble goby, coral snapper. Off the dock. She's counting. She can count to three.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: She ate the butterperch first. That means yes. The goby's for later and the snapper's for looking at.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: She's your boat's cat now. When the boat's stopped she'll hook fish out for you. She eats some. That's her wages.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: Watch her tail when you're fishing. It goes before the float does. She knows already. She always knows already.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: You've the kettle, and Mara's had her flounder. That's the bay, as far as coins will take you.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: North-west, past Gull Point, a belfry stands in the sea with its bell still in it. The water took the church. It left the bell.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Go and look at it. Only look. I'll tell you the rest when you've seen it's real.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: North-west, past Gull Point. A belfry standing in the sea. You can't miss it. I've tried.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: So it's still there. Good. Some tides it isn't.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: The keepers ring it when the bay has given all it has. The tide turns. The islands forget, and start again kinder.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: You won't forget. That's the keeper's share. Here, this was hers. It makes no sound, so mind who you blow it at.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: When you're ready, ring it. Your catch is sold and your coins go out with the tide. So does what coins did to your gear: the tuning, the creel, the bait.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: What you keep: your rods, her things, your boat, your journal. And the Echoes. The more the tide carried, the more of them come back.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: No hurry. You'll know the day. It's the day the stall has nothing left you want.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: The bell's where you left it, north-west past Gull Point. Ring it when the stall has nothing left you want.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Morning. First time out here? No. No, I know you. I nearly always do.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Those are Echoes in your satchel. Spend them. They're the only coin that stays spent.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: The fog's thinner on the far side of a Turning. Not thin enough to sail through. Thin enough to see where the road was.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: There was a road once, out through the fog. Iron lights, two lines of them, all the way to the Fen. They went out. Lights do.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: A fog lamp would wake them. Keepers kept one on the bow. It burns what the Bell gives back, so coins won't buy it. Echoes will.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Eight of them. Look in your satchel, where the Echoes are. I'd tell you where the last lamp went, but I think it was on her boat.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: The lamp wants eight Echoes. If you're short, the Bell has more. It always has more.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: There she is, on the bow. She'll light herself when the fog comes close. Don't help her. She doesn't like it.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: The road starts past the belfry, north-west. Two dead lights standing in the sea. Sail between them, and keep between them.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Off the road the fog is the fog still. It'll turn you round and tell you it was your idea.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: The Fen's the next water round. Green and still. Shallow enough to stand in, and deep enough not to.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: There's a doctor out there, counting things. Came through on the packet before the lights went out. That can't be right, can it? Never mind.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Mara's a box on the landing, so you needn't sail home to sell. Tell the doctor the ferryman remembers her. She'll say we've not met.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Past the belfry, north-west, between the two lights. Keep to the road. The doctor's on the landing at the far end.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: A visitor! Splendid. Dr. Ines Calloway, natural history. Mind the tape, it's measuring.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: The ferryman remembers me? How kind. We've not met. I came out on the packet, which, yes, does not run. I have decided not to mind.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Now. You fish, and I measure. The fen keeps coming out a different size, and I should like a second opinion.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: She wants a mast, a suit of sails and a great deal of paint. I want forty thousand. One of us will be disappointed, and it won't be her.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: She'll carry more than the skiff and go quicker, and there's room aboard for two besides you. She draws more water, mind. The reeds will tell you where.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Forty thousand for the Puffin. Ask me about the boatyard. The skiff stays yours. I'll mind whichever you're not sailing.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: There. She floats. She's a little surprised, I think. So am I.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: I put the moorhen's nest back on the bar. She watched me do it. She'll be telling the reeds.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: My brother's name is on the tiller still, underneath. Don't sand it. I can't read it either.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: First, a baseline. I need to know what a fish of this fen weighs when nobody is being clever about it.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Catch me six. Any sort, anywhere in the fen. I shall weigh them and write the numbers down, and we shall see if they stay written.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Sell them in Mara's box after. It gives stall prices. I have had it in pieces twice, and it is a box.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Six fish of the fen, any sort. I've the scale ready. It was ready before you came, which I don't remember doing.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Six. Thank you. Now watch the scale. There. And again. You saw that?

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: The same fish, a quarter of a pound heavier the second time. I am a careful woman. I do not think it is me.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Glasswater next. The lagoon in the middle, west of here. Clear as a lens, and I want to know what it magnifies.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: There's a little fish there you can see straight through. Glassfin. Bring me one whole. Try a mayfly on the hook.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: A Glassfin, from Glasswater. West of here, the still lagoon. You'll see the bottom all the way out.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Lovely. Hold it to the light. You can read through it. I've tried: my own notes, quite legible.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Except this line. I didn't write that. 'She is on the far side.' It's in my hand. Well. I shall press it flat and think.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: I ran a line across the Reed Maze, north of here. A stake at each end, and my best tape between.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: It was two hundred yards when I set it. Sail up and read me the far stake, the one on the long bar. I can't leave the scale.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Mind the reed beds. The channels go round them, and so must you.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: The far stake, on the long bar in the Reed Maze. North of here. Just read me the number.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Two hundred and forty? You're sure. No, I believe you. I believe the tape. That's what worries me.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Forty yards of fen that were not there on Tuesday. It isn't growing. Growing leaves marks. It's being remembered larger.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Here, you'll want a hat for this sun. That one's my spare. The tape in the band is not to be trusted either.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: While you were at the stake, did you see a boat? West of it, on the flats. A fat little sloop with her mast down. I take bearings off her.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: She has PUFFIN on the transom and a moorhen in the cockpit. She has not moved in my time, which is more than I can say for the fen.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Your ferryman would know whose she was. Look her over, and ask him. I should like one thing out here to have an explanation.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: The sloop on the flats, west of my stake in the Reed Maze. Bring the skiff alongside and look her over. Then ask your ferryman.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: The Puffin. My brother's. He took her into the Fen for eels the autumn the fog came down, and he walked home. He never said how.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: A moorhen in the cockpit? Good. They won't nest in a boat that's finished. I can float her off and fit her out.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Forty thousand, and that's a brother's price. Ask me about the boatyard. I haven't got one. I shall have by the time you ask.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: The trees in the west light up after dark. The moss does, I mean. So does something in the water under them.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Glowbelly, the reed-cutters called it. Nobody has brought me one. Go at night, to the Standing Trees, and put something that glows on the hook.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: A Glowbelly, after dark, under the Standing Trees. West, past Glasswater. A glowgrub on the hook wouldn't hurt.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Oh, look at it. Into the jar. Now cover the jar. Still lit! It isn't reflecting anything. It's making it.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: It brightens when I talk. Not when you do. Say something. No. Only me. How very flattering, and I do not like it at all.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: South-west of the lagoon there's a hole. The Sump. I put a lead down it on four hundred fathoms of line.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: It didn't touch. It's still going, as far as I know. I cut it loose on the third day.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Something lives in it. Long. I want to know how long. You'll need your strongest rod, and a worm.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: The Sump. South-west of Glasswater, where the water goes dark. A strong rod and a marsh worm.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Hold the tail. I'll take the head. Five feet two. Now you hold the head. Six feet. Don't look at me like that.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: I think it's the same with the fen. It is as big as whoever is measuring. And somebody a good deal bigger than us has started.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Last one, and it isn't a measurement. On the far side, north-west past the trees, there's a platform on piles. Somebody built it to sit and listen.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: There's a brass ear trumpet on it the size of a dinghy, pointed down at the water. I put my ear to it once. Once.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: You go. You've the look of somebody it would rather talk to. There's a tin box by the stool. Bring me what's in it.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: The Listening Post. North-west, past the trees, as far as the fen goes. Put your ear to the trumpet. Then come back.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: A page. One page, and the rest of the book gone. 'I. Fenn.' Do you know the name? No. Nor do I, and I keep nearly knowing it.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: She sat there and wrote down what the water said. Read the last line. 'It is not the fish that listen.' Keep it. It was left for you, not for me.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: And if something with no eyes comes up by the post at night, don't tell me how big it was. I shan't be able to stop myself.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: There is a gentleman on the sea-road. By the eighth light out from this end, standing on the water, with a bag. I have counted him four nights running.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: He is waiting for the packet. I had not the heart to tell him, and I rather think he would not hear it. He is mostly fog.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Offer him a berth, would you? One of his own. He will not sit where a cat has sat. He was most particular, and I have not got a cat.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: The eighth light out along the sea-road, on your right hand as you leave. He wants a berth of his own. He was most particular.

lines.speaker: Mister Hollis
lines.voiceStyle: elderly gentleman, slow and courteous, soft and a little far away, as if heard through fog
lines.text: Good evening. You are not the packet. No. But you have a seat, and I have been standing some time.

lines.speaker: Mister Hollis
lines.voiceStyle: elderly gentleman, slow and courteous, soft and a little far away, as if heard through fog
lines.text: Hollis. I shall pay my passage in fish, if fish are acceptable. I keep a line in the bag. After dark, you understand. By day I am not at my best.

lines.speaker: Mister Hollis
lines.voiceStyle: elderly gentleman, slow and courteous, soft and a little far away, as if heard through fog
lines.text: Pray do not trouble about the hour. It was a quarter past when I arrived, and I see it is a quarter past still.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Tide's kind today. Don't waste it talking to me.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Butterperch fry up lovely. Not that I'd know. I'm far too busy.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: If you see a light out past the Teeth, don't row toward it. Just… don't.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Your rod's older than you are. Treat it gently.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: You've the look of someone I've sold a rod to. I haven't, have I? No. Never mind me.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: I wrote your name in the book this morning, before you'd said it. Odd, that.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Somebody's been at my prices in the night. Everything's back where it started.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: High water at a quarter past never. Low water just after you've forgotten.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: The lamp remembers. That's the trouble with lamps.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Mind the second moon. It minds you.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Tide's turned. You'll have noticed. Nobody else will.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: You again. For the first time.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: The bell's quiet this morning. That's how you know it rang.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: I'm drawing a fish with nine eyes. No, ten. It keeps changing.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: Biscuit ate my blue crayon. Now everything's a bit green.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: Did you know fish dream? I asked one. It said yes.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: I drew you yesterday. But I only met you today. Look, it's even got your hat.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: Biscuit knows you. Biscuit doesn't know anybody.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: Everything's new again. I like new. I think I've liked it lots of times.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Fourteen paces from the hut to the jetty. Yesterday it was twelve. I have not grown shorter.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Do not lean on the theodolite. It is pointing at something, and I should like to know what.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: The frogs stop all at once, you know. Every evening. As if somebody had raised a hand.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: Have we met? No. And yet I have left room for you in the margin. How very like me.

lines.speaker: Dr. Ines Calloway
lines.voiceStyle: brisk, cheerful, practical woman in her forties; clipped, precise, quick to laugh
lines.text: My notebook has your catches in it, dated next week. I shall assume I was being optimistic.

lines.speaker: Mister Hollis
lines.voiceStyle: elderly gentleman, slow and courteous, soft and a little far away, as if heard through fog
lines.text: Good evening. I am waiting for the packet. She is a little behind her time. Forty years, I am told, but one does not like to fuss.

lines.speaker: Mister Hollis
lines.voiceStyle: elderly gentleman, slow and courteous, soft and a little far away, as if heard through fog
lines.text: I should be glad of a seat, when there is one going. I do not take up much room. Less by day.

lines.speaker: Mister Hollis
lines.voiceStyle: elderly gentleman, slow and courteous, soft and a little far away, as if heard through fog
lines.text: Is that the packet's light? No. It is yours. Forgive me. One hopes.

lines.speaker: Mister Hollis
lines.voiceStyle: elderly gentleman, slow and courteous, soft and a little far away, as if heard through fog
lines.text: Have we been introduced? I feel sure I have declined your kind offer before. More than once. How tiresome for you.
